title: On Reward-Balancing Methods for Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper investigates the so-called reward-balancing methods, a novel class of algorithms for solving discounted-return reinforcement learning (RL) problems. These methods consist of iteratively adjusting the reward function to transform the RL problem into an equivalent one in which the optimal policies are greedy. For this procedure, referred to as normalization process, we provide a theoretical analysis of the involved transformations, emphasizing their algebraic structure.
